checklist.notes: The short present-simple statements, personal-information questions, guided dialogue, and basic /v/ and /z/ practice are suitable for A1.1 learners.

The rule "After he/she, add -s: lives or studies" is inaccurate: "studies" requires changing consonant + y to -ies rather than simply adding -s, and the third-person-singular scope also includes "it" and singular noun subjects.
The material stays within the declared present-simple, personal-information, four-skill, and introductory phoneme targets; it does not introduce a clearly out-of-scope structure.
The model dialogue answers the stated questions appropriately, the form key contains correct surface forms, and the static recording, replay, and self-check instructions are internally actionable.

Most learner-facing language is natural, but the title "Foundational exchange: foundations" is tautological and awkward, and "Do not add another beat after it" is less clear than explicitly warning against adding an extra vowel sound.

No suspiciously distinctive borrowed passage is apparent in this brief static artifact, but originality cannot be established without external comparison; no Internet-wide originality conclusion is made.

findings.description: The lesson explicitly says to add -s after he/she while presenting "studies" as an example, concealing the required consonant-plus-y spelling change and giving an incomplete account of third-person-singular subjects.
findings.recommendation: Replace the rule with a bounded accurate formulation such as: "With he, she, it, or one person or thing, use the third-person form. Usually add -s (live → lives); after a consonant + y, change y to -ies (study → studies)."

findings.description: The title "Foundational exchange: foundations" is repetitive, and "another beat" is an imprecise description of the unwanted vowel after final /z/.
findings.recommendation: Use a specific title such as "Talking about facts and routines" and say "Do not add an extra vowel sound after /v/ or /z/."
